One-page note · September 2026

Data & methodology

Purpose. The Cabo Verde Municipal Opportunity Explorer is a screening tool for comparing the country’s 22 municipalities. It helps a user identify places that may merit deeper investigation for connectivity, digital services, commercial access, or inclusion initiatives. It is a prioritization aid—not an investment forecast.

Dataset and preparation

The published CSV contains one record per municipality and 14 fields covering population, housing, employment, age, education, mobile use, internet use, area, and population density. The site maps municipality codes to readable names and groups municipalities by island for display.

The working source included a large blank-row tail. The presentation layer keeps the 22 populated records and excludes empty rows. Numeric fields are parsed as numbers; the municipal code remains text. No missing values are imputed. The source file does not identify a reference year, collection instrument, or complete provenance chain, so the interface flags the year as unknown.

Calculated indicators

  • Internet penetration: internet users ÷ population × 100.
  • Mobile penetration: mobile users ÷ population × 100.
  • Digital gap: max(0, population − internet users).
  • Observed unemployment: unemployed ÷ (employed + unemployed) × 100.
  • School participation: attending ÷ (attending + never attended) × 100.
  • Mobile–internet conversion gap: max(0, mobile penetration − internet penetration).

Opportunity score

Six components are normalized to a 0–1 range across the 22 municipalities. Population, digital gap, density, and employment use log-transformed values before min–max normalization to reduce the dominance of extreme values. Conversion gap and the education-opportunity measure are min–max normalized directly.

Score = 25% market size + 20% digital gap + 15% density + 15% employment base + 15% mobile–internet gap + 10% education opportunity

The simulator lets users change these weights through strategy presets or sliders. Scores are therefore relative to this dataset and the selected assumptions; they are not absolute measures of municipal performance.

Quality checks

  • Verified 22 non-empty municipal records.
  • Preserved the original source columns in the downloadable CSV.
  • Recomputed ratios in the browser from the displayed values.
  • Avoided a geographic boundary map because no verified boundary file is included.

Known limitations

  • No confirmed date, sampling method, or source lineage in the file.
  • No income, prices, competition, coverage quality, cost, or infrastructure-capacity data.
  • Counts may describe different universes or definitions.
  • Normalization makes rankings sensitive to outliers and to the set of municipalities included.
Interpretation rule. Treat a high score as a prompt for field validation and additional research—not as proof of demand, profitability, need, or causal impact.

Reproducibility: the downloadable dataset, formulas above, visible weights, and client-side code provide an auditable path from each source value to the dashboard’s calculated indicators and rankings.
